sources.name: Linux kernel fs-verity documentation
sources.finding: fs-verity authenticates file contents on reads/mmap against a Merkle tree after verity enablement and makes the file read-only, but trusted userspace must still authenticate the expected digest and reject replacement/non-verity files. It is content-integrity evidence, not process-consumption or path-identity proof.

sources.name: openat2(2)
sources.finding: dirfd-anchored resolution with RESOLVE_BENEATH/NO_SYMLINKS/NO_XDEV can constrain pathname traversal during file acquisition.

sources.name: execveat(2)
sources.finding: AT_EMPTY_PATH can execute the executable referred to by an already-open fd; useful for native binaries, but insufficient to bind a multi-file Python import graph.

sources.name: memfd_create(2)
sources.finding: memfd sealing can prevent later modification of an already-populated in-memory file and is a possible cross-process TOCTOU hardener.

sources.name: F2 release_integrity.py
sources.finding: F2 already has FRANKENSTEIN2_RELEASE_MANIFEST/v1 binding release_id, source_commit, source_tree, build_id and per-file canonical path/SHA-256/size while rejecting symlink payload entries.

sources.name: F2 portable_release_transaction.py
sources.finding: F2-WP-1207 already binds artifact_sha256/manifest_sha256 and explicit state/release lineage, but remains preparatory and grants no target-runtime credit.

sources.name: F2 portable_release_readback.py
sources.finding: F2-WP-1207 generation 2 verifies that the observed active release digest equals the planned target release digest, but explicitly remains preparatory and does not prove which package bytes a Python process consumed.

conclusion: Do not make fs-verity a mandatory F2 exact-source prerequisite. Reuse the existing ReleaseManifest and WP1207 release readback as the artifact/release identity substrate, then add a minimal same-bytes consumption witness at the loader/import boundary. fs-verity may remain an optional host-supported defense-in-depth signal.
